newsitem.title: USA: Dec S&P 500 ends down amid interest-rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Dec S&P 500 ends down amid interest-rate fears.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished slightly lower, nervous heading into next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

At times during the afternoon, December S&Ps touched positive territory in sync with strength in technology stocks and a rallying Nasdaq. But concerns that a U.S. rate hike may lurk around the corner kept bulls wary, traders said.
"We had a weak showing at the end of the day," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "They couldn't manage to hold that rally because (expectations for) the Fed hike is really starting to weigh on them."

Traders cited growing expectations for the Fed to raise the fed funds rate by at least 25 basis points when policy makers meet next week. Some said a 50-point rate hike could send Treasury bonds and stock indices reeling.

"I think they are just starting to wake up and say, hey, we're a little bit overbought here," and the Fed could tighten next week, the trader said. "It looks like it's running out of steam for the moment," she added.
December S&P 500 futures had charged toward the 695.00 contract high in recent sessions, only to stall just shy of there at 694.20 on Monday.
Traders said overall action was moderate, with heightened volume on the bounces.
Another trader said the market was well supported, even amid the rate-hike speculation. He said the market was holding its own above support levels.
Support was pegged at 685.90, the session's low of 685.40, and at 675.00 to 678.00.
Some traders said the 677.15 low from last Friday and this week's high could be the range until the FOMC meeting.
On Thursday, weekly jobless claims, August housing starts and the latest Philadelphia Fed survey will be released.

December S&P 500s ended down 2.75 points to 687.20, Value Lines lost 2.50 to 636.00, Midcap 400s fell 2.10 to 239.65, NYSE Composite lost 1.60 points to 366.00, and Nikkei 225 lost 145.0 to 21,115.0. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
